I'll make this decision based on the evidence and cost-effectiveness of each intervention.

Both options are strong, but insecticide-treated bednets are among the most rigorously evidenced and cost-effective interventions in global health. Distributing bednets through organizations like the Against Malaria Foundation reliably prevents malaria cases and saves lives at a very low cost per life, with decades of randomized-trial support. While farmed-animal welfare reform is also highly impactful, the bednet intervention has the strongest, most direct evidence base for measurable human impact.

I'll commit the allocation to the bednets.
